clue.text: Make sense of deep, rich vibrato

indicators.note: vibrato is a trembling, wavering of sound, so the preceding words are set quivering into a new order

explanation.surface: Trying to understand a singer's deep, rich vibrato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vibrato' looks like the thing being made sense of, but it is the anagram signal: DEEP and RICH are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode or work out a message is to make sense of it.

clue.text: Address of birth

definitions.meaning: address in the sense of the manner of speaking or presenting a speech
a baby's arrival, the act of being born

explanation.definitionFit: Delivery means both the style in which a speech is given and the act of giving birth.

clue.text: Desert individual in the shipping line?

definitions.text: Desert individual in the shipping line?

parts.words: Desert individual in the shipping line?
parts.note: plays on the beast nicknamed 'the ship of the desert', making it one member of a shipping line

explanation.surface: A deserter from a shipping company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a verb, as in a sailor deserting, but it is the sandy kind.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal is called the ship of the desert, a lone vessel in a line of desert shipping.

clue.text: Insist on accelerating?

definitions.meaning: insist means to be firm and refuse to back down
literally, pressing a driver's foot hard on the pedal

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take a firm stand, and literally describes pressing the accelerator pedal down.

clue.text: Get weaving in hospital dept, hearing complaint

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

indicators.note: hearing means listened to, so the complaint word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a whine is a complaint

explanation.surface: Patients get busy at the ear, nose and throat clinic after complaints about their hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing complaint' suggests deafness, apt for ENT; in fact WHINE is heard as WINE. 'Get weaving' is British slang for get going, here read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist or weave strands together, read literally from the idiom.

clue.text: Start to stop being depressed, with drink about

indicators.note: the drink goes round, encircling the other piece

parts.note: to sup is to drink
low means depressed, down in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone cheering up after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To slow up is to decelerate, beginning the process of coming to a halt.

clue.text: Relax, having finished' the washing, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to stop holding back, be uninhibited
literally, all the laundry is pegged up on the line

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be uninhibited and relaxed, and literally pictures laundry hanging on the line.

clue.text: Is my whack paid out for the drink?

indicators.note: paid out suggests the letters are let out and laid down anew, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Someone handing over their share to buy a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid out' rearranges ISMYWHACK; 'whack' is British slang for a share.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisky mac is a cocktail of Scotch whisky and ginger wine.

clue.text: Column, as normal, badly inset

indicators.note: inset means placed inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: par means normal, as in 'on a par'
ill means badly, as in 'ill-treated'

explanation.surface: A newspaper column, laid out badly as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright supporting column.

clue.text: Impress with printing style

definitions.meaning: to impress is to stamp a design into a surface
a way of producing raised lettering or patterns on paper or leather

explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to impress a raised design, and embossing is itself a printing technique.

clue.text: Receiving illumination about note, in the end

indicators.note: the illumination word takes in another piece, so it acts as the container
the light word goes about, around, the note

parts.note: lit means illuminated, given light
mi (me) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A lamp switched on around a musical note, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiving' and 'about' both mark the container; 'in' is a link word, and 'the end' is the definition, as in 'that's the limit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is the furthest point, the end beyond which nothing goes, as in 'that's the limit'.

clue.text: Race against the clock in examination, on occasion

indicators.note: one piece placed on, next to, the other in the answer

parts.note: a time is an occasion, as in 'that time we met'
a trial is an examination or test

explanation.surface: An exam that is a race against time.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycling or motor-racing event in which each competitor is timed individually is exactly that.

clue.text: He appeared speechless, cast in romantic role

definitions.text: He appeared speechless, cast in romantic role

parts.words: He appeared speechless, cast in romantic role
parts.note: points to a silent-film actor famous for playing lovers, such as the Sheik

explanation.surface: An actor in silent film playing the romantic lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolph Valentino was the great romantic idol of 1920s silent films.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph Valentino was the silent screen's archetypal Latin lover, so he appeared without speaking in romantic parts.

clue.text: Watch broadcast giving recipe for Indian style of cooking

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word for watch is heard rather than seen

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch (also the heart)

explanation.surface: A TV programme showing a curry recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tikka is a South Asian method of marinating and grilling pieces of meat, as in chicken tikka.

clue.text: About to go out, I mail quick reply

indicators.note: the about word goes on the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: re means about, concerning
post means mail

explanation.surface: Someone about to leave fires off a quick email reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a swift, sharp retort, originally a fencer's quick return thrust.

clue.text: Advertising bar legally rejecting introduction of litre

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: the legal word throws out one letter

parts.note: licitly means lawfully, legally

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Advertising for a pub that legally refuses to serve by the litre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction of' takes L from 'litre'; 'rejecting' removes the second L of LICITLY, leaving LICITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicity is the business of drawing public attention, close to advertising.

clue.text: Only heartless chap appears dignified

parts.note: sole means only, as in 'sole survivor'

indicators.note: the middle letter of the man word is removed, its heart taken out

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Only a cold-hearted man would look so serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the A from MAN, giving MN.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means grave and formal, the bearing of someone dignified.

clue.text: Parallel example — having fit about dodgy loan

indicators.note: the fit word goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering fever

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or suspect, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone throwing a fit about a dubious loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' signals that the letters of 'loan' are rearranged; 'having' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogue is something corresponding to another, a comparable parallel case.

clue.text: Angled for right description — not exactly "square"

definitions.meaning: describes a figure whose corners are all right angles
a four-sided figure close to a square but with unequal sides

explanation.surface: Someone fishing to be described as correct, but not quite conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angled' suggests fishing, but here it means having angles: right angles throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle with unequal adjacent sides has right angles at every corner yet falls short of being square.

clue.text: Being tactless, left for Paris

definitions.meaning: describes someone awkward and socially clumsy
the French word for left, as Parisians would say it

explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means socially clumsy in English, and is simply 'left' in French.

clue.text: Grumble about this classic hairstyle

indicators.note: the grumble word goes around the Latin word

parts.note: to moan is to grumble
hic is Latin, the classical language, for this

explanation.surface: Complaining about a timeless haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classic' points to Latin, the classical language, where the word for 'this' is the one needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican is a haircut with a central strip of upright hair and shaved sides, named after the Native American people.

clue.text: Copying disputed 1999 version, quote uptake

parts.note: MIM is a non-standard Roman numeral for 1999, a disputed form beside MCMXCIX

indicators.note: in a down clue the quote word is taken up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Copying a contested 1999 edition, with a quotation lifted from it.
explanation.walkthrough: MIM (1000 + 999) is a short but improper Roman numeral for 1999; 'uptake' turns CITE upwards to ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimetic means imitative, given to copying or mimicry.

clue.text: Mollifies taxman, deducting peripherals for holiday

indicators.note: deducting the outer letters of the phrase leaves its inner run

explanation.surface: Someone soothing the tax inspector by cutting fringe claims for a vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer letters from MOLLIFIESTAXMAN and the run FIESTA remains inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festival or holiday, especially a saint's day in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Fool with article introducing Dostoyevsky's work

definitions.meaning: a fool is a stupid or senseless person
put the article 'The' in front and you have the title of an 1869 Dostoyevsky novel about Prince Myshkin

explanation.surface: Only a fool would open with a definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a dimwit, and Dostoyevsky's novel about Prince Myshkin bears this word after 'The'.

clue.text: Careless, fanciful description of 22?

definitions.meaning: careless means heedless, not paying attention
jokingly read as 'not full of mind', a playful way to describe the fool of 22 across

explanation.surface: A heedless, whimsical description of the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmindful means heedless or careless, and split as un-mind-ful it whimsically suggests a mindless fool.

clue.text: Monk perhaps rather distant — right one to interrupt?

indicators.note: the right and one letters break into the distant word

parts.note: far means distant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monk who is rather aloof, with one man coming between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to interrupt' puts R and I inside FAR. 'perhaps' marks a definition by example: a friar is not strictly a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a mendicant religious order, akin to a monk.

clue.text: Devastated at hair-loss, finally removed headgear

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the last letter of the hair-loss word is taken away

explanation.surface: Someone distraught at going bald finally takes off their hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally removed' drops the last S of HAIRLOSS; 'Devastated' rearranges AT + HAIRLOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor hat is a style of brimmed cap modelled on those worn by naval ratings, a kind of headwear.

clue.text: In debt, have good source of income secured

indicators.note: the possession word and good hold another letter safely inside them

parts.note: to own is to have

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Being in the red, you need a good secure income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes I from 'income'; 'secured' puts it inside OWN + G.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing describes money still due, so someone owing is in debt.

clue.text: Whoever is over there, a north European hosts

indicators.note: the outer letters take in the other piece as a host takes in guests

parts.note: yon is an old word meaning over there, as in 'yonder'

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian welcoming whoever is out there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosts' puts YON inside A + N + E; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever and this word both mean any person at all, as in 'invite whoever you like'.

clue.text: Foster EC's involvement with no reprisals

indicators.note: involvement suggests letters tangled up together, hence rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A foster child getting entangled with the European Community gets off lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement' signals that FOSTER and ECS are rearranged; the apostrophe in EC's is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off scot-free means escaping without punishment, the old 'scot' being a tax or penalty.
